newsitem.title: USA: Neurogen still backs schizophrenia drug.
newsitem.headline: Neurogen still backs schizophrenia drug.

text.p: Neurogen Corp said Wednesday that results from its Phase I human clinical trials of its dopamine D4 antagonist drug for schizophrenia, NGD 94-4, have shown the drug to be be safe and well tolerated across a broad dose range.

However, the company said the interim human data suggest that the drug is more quickly metabolized in humans than had been expected, based upon preclinical studies conducted in primates by Schering-Plough Corp.
This, said Neurogen, raises questions as to whether it has the desirable pharmacokinetic profile those studies suggested.
The company said, however, that it remained committed to the D4/schizophrenia hypothesis and very confident that it will bring the right compound forward.

Neurogen said it is still too early to pronounce judgment on NGD 94-4, and that it will examine the data with Schering-Plough to address the pharmacokinetics issues raised by the study. The company added that a number of other collaboration compounds are being reviewed as a possible replacement.

The company also said that it had received notice from Schering-Plough of its intention to extend the research collaboration between the companies covering drugs to treat schizophrenia through June 1998.

Schering-Plough's extension of the collaboration with Neurogen, said the company, is effective for the period from July, 1997 through June, 1998, pending adoption of a formal research plan relating to the extension period.

The extension could bring it up to $3.6 million in additional research funding. Including $6 million Neurogen has received for access to a portion of its combinatorial library, Neurogen has received to date $27 million of the potential $70 million collaboration.
